title: LumaCart Q4 Inference Sprint Readout & Constraints Sync
summary: Quarterly operational readout focused on recent inference sprint outcomes: usage spike during holiday promo, unexpected tail latency on image2text pipeline, cost variance vs forecast, and next steps for a targeted pilot (Dedicated capacity vs private VPC). Agreed to run a short benchmark, share security/compliance docs, and scope a 4-week pilot with committed capacity if metrics hit targets.
topics: Holiday promo usage spike and burst behavior
Tail latency on image2text and batch sizing
Cost variance and token accounting (embedding vs gen)
Security posture: SSO, KMS, audit logs

transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2025-12-03 16:00 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya, Hector, Priya (Redwood); Evan, Sara, Marco, Leah, Jonas (LumaCart)

Auto Summary (auto): We went over the spike, saw tail latency on the image2text pipeline, chatted about configs (batch size, prefix cache), and landed on bench + pilot.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood, Hector our SE, Priya on CS. LumaCart team?
[00:06] Evan (Head of ML): Evan here. Sara, Marco, Leah, Jonas too. Thanks Maya.
[00:10] Maya: Cool. Agenda — runthrough of the sprint outcomes, the holiday promo spike, latency/cost anomalies, and then pilot scoping. Anything else to add?
[00:18] Sara (VP Eng): No, that's fine. We mostly want to understand root cause and get a plan for production resiliency.
[00:25] Hector (SE): Great. So quick recap from Redwood side — we pulled the traces you shared, saw the image2text model had a long-tail at 99th percentile when QPS rose over 180. There's also repeated KV cache misses which amplify per-request compute. Note: some of the field names in your export showed K-V cash misses — transcription on our side, sorry.
[00:42] Jonah? Jonas (SRE): Jonas — yes that lines up with what we saw, the edge workers seemed to thrash under bursts and our autoscale delay made things worse.
[00:50] Leah (Data Platform): Also saw more small requests hitting generation API vs embeddings — it's inflating token counts, we think some of the telemetry double-counts prompt metadata.
[01:02] Hector: Right — we flagged that a bit. There's a difference in cost accounting for generation calls (token-in/out) vs embedding units; small text->embed patterns can look cheaper but in aggregate they add up because of metadata.
[01:15] Evan: So main asks — how do we keep latency under SLO during promos without doubling spend?
[01:22] Maya: Two levers: smarter batching + prefix/KV caching, and routing to Dedicated pools for hot traffic. Dedicated gives more predictable tail latencies but requires commit. Private VPC is available too if you need peering and KMS control.
[01:35] Sara: Can you remind us of the tradeoffs? We got a slide in the last deck but want the TL;DR.
[01:40] Hector: Sure. Hosted (Redwood API) -> lowest operational lift, variable costs. Dedicated -> reserved GPU pools, predictable tail latency, better isolation, slightly lower unit cost at scale. Private/VPC -> full network control, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs; adds setup overhead and ops responsibility. With Dedicated you can configure autoscale policies and burst buckets.
[02:03] Marco: Our security team will push back on non-VPC for PCI-ish flows; we need KMS and SSO via SAML. How mature are your KMS integrations?
[02:12] Priya (CSM): We support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments; for Dedicated we offer integration with cloud KMS and customer keys. SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported across the Console, and we can share the SOC2/ISO pack.
[02:28] Sara: Good. We care about audit logs for all inference calls — is that enabled by default?
[02:33] Hector: Audit logs are available on Dedicated/Private with configurable retention. Hosted has request-level logs but redaction options for PII. We'll send details.
[02:44] Evan: About the spike — do you think the batching config could have prevented the long tail?
[02:48] Hector: Possibly. From traces, average sequence length was short but arrival pattern was very bursty. With continuous batching and a slightly higher latency SLO you can improve throughput and reduce per-token cost. But for 99th percentile latency, Dedicated with smaller batch windows helps more. There's a tradeoff: larger batches reduce cost, smaller batches reduce tail latency.
[03:12] Sara: We ran a quick A/B yesterday between two endpoints — one with larger batching and one with immediate flush. Larger batching saved cost but saw spikes in 95th/99th.
[03:23] Jonas: Our problem was the autoscaler threshold takes 60s to spin a new worker, so the first minute of a burst is painful.
[03:29] Maya: We can help tune autoscale policy at the infra layer — e.g., keep a small warm pool during promos and use burst capacity. That reduces the cold-start tail.
[03:36] Leah: Any quick wins?
[03:38] Hector: Short-term: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (we saw many identical prefix tokens in the dataset), tune batch windows for the image2text route to a middle-ground, and increase warm pool during known promos. Medium-term: consider Dedicated pilot for hot routes.
[03:54] Evan: How do we measure pilot success? We need clear metrics.
[03:58] Priya: We proposed success criteria: 99th pctl latency under 700ms during a 2x baseline traffic spike, token cost variance under +15% vs baseline, and no missed audit logs. Also operational checklist for KMS and SSO.
[04:18] Sara: That sounds reasonable. What about the cost model? We saw a 28% increase MoM in the last two weeks.
[04:25] Maya: From our initial look, the increase is driven by two factors: more gen calls counted as full sequences because of prompt metadata, and some workflows shifted from short embeddings to generation. We'll share the cost breakdown spreadsheet with per-route token counts and suggested quantization/packing.
[04:42] Evan: Is quantization something we can do without breaking quality for image2text?
[04:47] Hector: Possibly — quantization profiles differ by model. For some models you get 2-4x throughput gains with minimal or acceptable quality degradation; we'd recommend running an eval suite against your prompts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles.
[04:59] Marco: For Private deployment, how long is setup usually? We're trying to line this up with a January security window.
[05:05] Priya: Private deploys typically take 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and key management. Dedicated is much faster — usually 1-2 weeks if networking is standard.
[05:17] Sara: Ok. If Dedicated can get us under SLO with an acceptable cost delta we'll prefer that to a full Private setup for now.
[05:24] Maya: Sounds like the plan. We'll run the bench and come back with numbers. Hector will attempt a short 1-hour simulated burst with your exact prompt set.
[05:32] Hector: Yes — I'll run a bench that mirrors your traffic shape (bursty, 3 min microbursts). I'll collect token counts, tail latency, and KV cache hit ratios.
[05:40] Jonas: Also please include the edge worker queue depth in logs so we can correlate autoscale behavior.
[05:44] Hector: Will do.
[05:46] Evan: Any worries about compliance during the pilot?
[05:49] Priya: We'll use redaction and controlled logs for the pilot; for an enterprise Private deploy we'll integrate your KMS and SSO from day one.
[05:58] Sara: Great. Can you also share a sample SLA and committed capacity offer for Dedicated?
[06:02] Maya: Yes, we'll send a draft commitment tiers sheet and SLA examples.
[06:08] Leah: One more thing — we noticed a few odd error patterns in the last run (400s), could that be rate-limiting?
[06:14] Hector: Possibly. The device logs showed a misrouted 429 vs 400 mapping in the proxy — small mapping bug. We'll attach the trace.
[06:22] Evan: Ok — let's recap next steps.
[06:24] Maya: Recap: Redwood runs bench (Hector), sends bench template and cost sheet (Maya), security docs (Priya). LumaCart provides VPC/IAM diagram, peak expected qps and test window, and confirms pilot go/no-go by 2025-12-12.
[06:41] Marco: We'll aim for that. 
[06:43] Sara: Thanks everyone. Schedule follow-up for a bench readout mid next week.
[06:48] Maya: Thanks, closing 52-minute call.

Questions (captured):
- How does Dedicated vs Private impact setup time? (Answered: Dedicated faster, Private 4-8 weeks)
- Can quantization be safe for image2text? (Answered: recommend evals)
- Are audit logs and KMS supported? (Answered: yes on Dedicated/Private; hosted limited but redaction)

Links/References Shared:
- benchmark_template.xlsx (link: shared in follow-up email)
- cost_breakdown_lumacart.csv (link: shared)
- SOC2 + private_deploy_security_pack.pdf (link: via secure link)

End of transcript.
